message.reasoning:
I'm mapping out the ZipArchiveEntry class structure, identifying the constructors and key getter/setter methods with branching logic that I'll need to cover in JUnit 4 tests.

I'm continuing to catalog the remaining methods around Unix mode handling, extra field management, and merge/copy operations, noting where conditionals like null checks and instanceof checks create branches I need to test.

Now I'm designing test cases and checking whether dependency classes like ZipShort, UnparseableExtraFieldData, and ZipExtraField implementations are available as real classes in the classpath rather than needing mocks, since these are part of the same module under test.

I'm planning out test methods covering constructors with names, directories, platform-specific backslash handling, and ZipEntry conversions. Since testing protected members requires package-level access, I'll place the test class in the same package as the source, org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.

From there I'm laying out further test cases for cloning, unix mode and symlink handling, attribute getters/setters, platform methods, and extra field parsing including edge cases with unparseable or empty data.

Continuing through more extra field tests covering additions, replacements, removals, and unparseable data handling, plus byte array setters for extra fields.

Then I'm listing tests around name handling — checking null names, directory detection, and how setName behaves differently based on platform (FAT vs non-FAT), whether backslashes get replaced, and edge cases like slashes already present or null input.

Continuing on, I'm covering size getters/setters with valid and negative values, raw name handling, hashCode, general purpose bit flags, extra field merging, last modified date, and a large batch of equals() tests checking identity, null, different classes, differing names/comments/times, and full equality. I'm also planning tests for version made by, version required, and raw flag getters/setters, aiming for comprehensive but manageable coverage.

Rather than relying on AsiExtraField's real parsing behavior for merge tests (which risks unpredictable failures), I'm deciding to build a simple custom test double implementing the ZipExtraField interface, so I have full control over its behavior for testing purposes.

Writing the test class...

Finishing the interface definition. I'll implement this as a custom static nested class in the test file to keep full control rather than relying on guessed external behavior, and I'm now checking whether UnparseableExtraFieldData is a real commons-compress class with a no-arg constructor.

Since I'm not certain of its exact constructor and internal storage, I'll rely only on what ZipArchiveEntry actually uses—checking `instanceof UnparseableExtraFieldData` and casting—rather than depending on undocumented internals.

To reduce risk, I'll instead test malformed extra field scenarios directly, like setting extra bytes with a header and length that doesn't fit the remaining data, to trigger the unparseable field handling path.

Actually, using ExtraFieldUtils.parse with UnparseableExtraField.READ mode is safer since it lets real parsing produce the UnparseableExtraFieldData instance rather than manually constructing it. I can pass a byte array too short to be valid, like three bytes when four are required for the header, to force it entirely into unparseable data.

So this gives me a clean way for tests to exercise the UnparseableExtraFieldData branch in addExtraField without directly constructing it -- I can just grab it via getUnparseableExtraFieldData() after feeding in malformed bytes.

Now I'm thinking through a simple test-double ZipExtraField implementation, "SimpleExtraField," to cover addExtraField, removeExtraField, getExtraField, and mergeExtraFields with both local=true and local=false cases, plus checking which imports (ZipExtraField, ZipShort, UnparseableExtraFieldData, ZipException) I'll actually need for these tests.

GeneralPurposeBit is a genuine class with a default constructor and equals/clone, so I don't need to dig into its internals -- just set and get values. I also recall UnixStat.LINK_FLAG as a real constant I can import directly, and I'm now laying out the test file's package declaration and import list.

I'll avoid mocking frameworks since I can just use real File objects instead -- creating a temp file with File.createTempFile for the regular file case, and using the system temp directory for the directory test case.

For the directory constructor test, I'm verifying that when passed an existing directory, ZipArchiveEntry appends a trailing slash to the entry name.

Since the source isn't a file, setSize never gets called, so the size stays at its default unknown value of -1, which I can check against the ArchiveEntry.SIZE_UNKNOWN constant.

For testing the regular file constructor, I'm creating a temp file and writing some bytes to it so I can verify a nonzero size gets picked up correctly, rather than just checking against an empty file.

Since the entry name won't end with a trailing slash and isFile() is true, setSize should use the file's actual length, so I'll assert getSize() equals f.length(). For the timestamp check, since ZipEntry rounds to 2-second precision, I'll skip exact equality and just verify the modified date is set rather than asserting a precise match.

Now I'm sketching out the clone() test: creating a ZipArchiveEntry with internal/external attributes and an extra field, cloning it, then asserting the clone preserves those attributes, matches extra field data, but isn't the same object reference. I'm also planning a test for setMethod with a negative value expecting an IllegalArgumentException, and starting a setUnixMode test for a non-directory writable file entry.

I'm working through the Unix permission bit math to verify the MS-DOS read-only attribute flag derived from the owner-write bit in the mode value 0100644.

To avoid ambiguity, I'll simplify with a plain mode like 0644 (no file type bits): mode&0200 is nonzero so read-only term is 0, and not a directory so that term is also 0. This gives externalAttributes = 420<<16 = 27525120, and getUnixMode() should correctly return 420 (0644) once platform is set to PLATFORM_UNIX.

For the read-only case, mode 0444 has no owner-write bit, so that adds a flag bit of 1 OR'd into the lower 16 bits alongside the shifted mode. Since getUnixMode() shifts right by 16, those low flag bits get discarded, leaving just the mode value—so the test should still see getUnixMode()==0444 regardless of the read-only flag.

I should also verify the low bit directly on externalAttributes to confirm the read-only flag was actually set. For directories, setUnixMode with mode 0755 on an entry named "dir/" should set the 0x10 directory bit in externalAttributes. For a fresh entry with default FAT platform, getUnixMode() should return 0 since setUnixMode was never called. For symlink detection, I'll set externalAttributes via setUnixMode using LINK_FLAG combined with mode 0644.

Now I'm writing tests for isUnixSymlink using UnixStat.LINK_FLAG combined with a permission mode, checking both true and false cases, then moving to test the protected getPlatform/setPlatform methods since the test class shares the same package.

For testing setExtraFields with unparseable data, I need to obtain an UnparseableExtraFieldData instance indirectly—by creating an entry, calling setExtra with malformed bytes to populate its internal field, then retrieving it via getUnparseableExtraFieldData() so I can pass it into another entry's setExtraFields() array alongside a normal field.

I'm verifying that getExtraFields() returns only the parseable one while getExtraFields(true) includes both, and that getUnparseableExtraFieldData() still returns the unparseable object. Then I'm checking the empty-array case, though I need to confirm whether setting an empty array should clear the unparseable data too.

Looking at the source logic, setExtraFields only overwrites unparseableExtra if a new UnparseableExtraFieldData instance is present in the passed array -- it never resets it to null otherwise. So testing with a fresh entry that has no unparseable data to begin with makes assertNull trivially true rather than actually verifying the reset behavior I want to check.

This is worth explicitly testing as a potential quirk: I should set unparseableExtra first via addExtraField, then call setExtraFields with only normal fields, and confirm whether the stale unparseableExtra value persists unexpectedly.

Still writing test assertions...

Now I want to verify how getExtraFields() behaves when extraFields is null on a fresh entry, tracing through the constructor logic to see when setExtraFields actually gets invoked.

So since extraFields is null, the equality check fails and the method just returns the shared static empty array directly rather than making a copy - that's a testable behavior for a fresh entry with no extras set.

But once extraFields becomes non-null (even an empty array), the equality check succeeds and getExtraFields returns a defensive copy each time. I can verify this by calling setExtraFields with an empty array, then calling getExtraFields twice and asserting the two returned arrays aren't the same reference.

Now I'm tracing through the branches for getAllExtraFieldsNoCopy and getUnparseableOnly depending on whether extraFields and unparseableExtra are null, so I can design a test for a fresh entry that has neither set, expecting zero-length results.

For the "only unparseable" test, I'm working out that setExtra with malformed data actually results in setExtraFields being called with the parsed array containing just an UnparseableExtraFieldData object, which means extraFields ends up as an empty array rather than staying null, while unparseableExtra gets set to that field — so my earlier assumption needs correcting.

Then tracing getAllExtraFieldsNoCopy with an empty extraFields array and a set unparseableExtra: it goes through getMergedFields, extending the array by one and placing the unparseable field at the end, giving a merged result of length one that matches what getCentralDirectoryExtra would produce. This lines up with the merged test case checking that the single returned field is exactly the unparseable data instance, and I'm now checking the copy branch to see if allExtraFieldsNoCopy equals extraFields.

To exercise the case where getAllExtraFieldsNoCopy returns extraFields directly (unparseableExtra null), I add a real extra field via addExtraField so extraFields becomes non-null with no unparseable data, then call getExtraFields(true) twice to confirm it returns distinct copies of length one each time, verifying the defensive copy behavior. Now I'm moving on to check the branches inside addExtraField itself.

For addExtraField, I need to cover: passing an UnparseableExtraFieldData instance (sets unparseableExtra without touching extraFields), starting from a null extraFields array (creates a fresh one-element array), and starting from a non-null array where the field either doesn't match an existing id (appends) or does match (removes the old one and replaces it). I'll write separate tests: adding the first field to a null array, appending a new distinct field, and replacing an existing field with the same header id.

I'm setting up test fixtures with a few SimpleExtraField instances sharing header ids to exercise the replace-vs-append logic, and thinking through how getExtraFields() returns a shallow copy so equality checks need to account for identity semantics of the field objects rather than relying on a custom equals method.

Adding the unparseable data confirms it's stored via getUnparseableExtraFieldData(). Now checking addAsFirstExtraField logic - it follows similar branching: unparseable fields get set directly, while normal fields check for existing matches to remove before copying the array.

I'm now considering the test cases: one verifies that adding a first extra field to a fresh entry with no existing fields results in a single-element array containing that field, and another checks that prepending a new field when one already exists (with no matching header) correctly places the new field at the front while preserving the old one.

I'm also working through the replacement case, where adding a field whose header matches an existing one removes the old field first before inserting the new one at the front, and the unparseable-data case, which just confirms that data gets stored and retrievable via the appropriate getter.

For removeExtraField, I'm planning tests: throwing NoSuchElementException when there are no fields at all, throwing when the target header isn't found, and correctly removing a matching field while confirming the remaining array and updated extra bytes. Now I'm moving on to removeUnparseableExtraField.

Testing that removing unparseable extra field data throws when none exists, and that setting malformed extra data followed by removal properly clears it. Then for getExtraField, I want cases covering found, not found with a null list, and not found with a populated list that has no match -- plus a simple direct test for getUnparseableExtraFieldData. I'm also noting that the setExtra(byte[]) exception path mentions a ZipException catch that's no longer reachable as of Compress 1.1.

I'm considering whether PowerMock, which appears to be on the classpath, could let me mock the static ExtraFieldUtils.parse method to force that ZipException and verify it gets wrapped into a RuntimeException, since triggering it through the plain API alone seems infeasible.

Writing PowerMock test class...

Adding remaining imports...

I also need to double-check the exact overload signature for ExtraFieldUtils.parse so the mocked static method matches correctly, particularly around the UnparseableExtraField parameter type.

For symmetry, I should add an analogous test for setCentralDirectoryExtra's catch block using the same mockStatic approach with local=false. Then I want to check the getLocalFileDataExtra branch where extra is already non-null.

Since the ZipArchiveEntry(String) constructor never explicitly sets extra unless setExtraFields or setExtra is called, a fresh entry's extra field defaults to null, so getLocalFileDataExtra() should return EMPTY. I'll write a test confirming that default behavior.

Then I need a test where a field is added via addExtraField, which internally calls setExtra, and verify getLocalFileDataExtra() returns non-empty merged bytes. I also want to sanity-check that getCentralDirectoryExtra() never returns null.

For getName(), I'm tracing whether the name==null branch is even reachable — since the constructor always calls setName (even the no-arg constructor delegates to this("")), the name field should always be non-null through the public API, making that null branch effectively dead code.

Since Whitebox from PowerMock's reflect utilities is on the classpath, I can use it to force the internal name field to null and then verify getName() falls back correctly to super.getName().

Now I'm moving on to test isDirectory by checking names ending or not ending with "/", and setName's branch involving FAT platform backslash replacement.

I'm working through more cases: verifying the constructor replaces backslashes with slashes when no "/" is present ("a\\b\\c" → "a/b/c"), confirming that a name already containing "/" leaves backslashes untouched, and adding a test for calling setName with null.

Since the test class shares the same package as ZipArchiveEntry, protected setName can be invoked directly without reflection, and I'm checking that passing null sets the name field accordingly rather than throwing.

Actually, since name becomes null, getName() falls back to the superclass's stored name, so the assertion should check that e.getName() returns the original "x" rather than null. This makes the reflection-based Whitebox test redundant, so I'll drop it and keep only this simpler direct test.

I also want to test the branch where platform isn't FAT—setting platform to UNIX and then calling setName with a backslash path should leave the name unchanged, since the replace-backslash logic only triggers for FAT platform.

Now I'm writing a test for the protected setName(String, byte[]) overload that accepts a raw byte array for the name.

I also need to cover the null branch of getRawName on a freshly constructed entry, verify hashCode matches the name's hashCode, and check that getGeneralPurposeBit/setGeneralPurposeBit properly store and retrieve (or clear to null) the GeneralPurposeBit object. Then I'm moving on to testing mergeExtraFields.

For the merge case, I need to test setExtra with local=true and setCentralDirectoryExtra with local=false, covering both branches: when no existing field matches the header (triggering addExtraField during merge) and when an existing field does match (triggering parseFromLocalFileData or parseFromCentralDirectoryData on that same object, confirming its data mutates in-place while the reference stays the same). The tricky part is that ExtraFieldUtils.parse only produces real known extra field types or UnparseableExtraFieldData for unrecognized data, so it won't generate my custom SimpleExtraField type -- I need another way to trigger that matching-header branch.

One option is to craft real bytes for a recognized extra field type like extended timestamp or AsiExtraField, but that adds byte-layout complexity. A simpler approach might work instead: add my SimpleExtraField manually via addExtraField, then call setExtra with parsed bytes that produce a real extra field type sharing the same header ID -- since header comparison relies on ZipShort value equality rather than object identity, the merge logic should still find and match my existing field.

Then I could try re-parsing those serialized bytes by calling setExtra with the field's own extra output again, but since the header ID is likely unrecognized by ExtraFieldUtils' registry, it would probably just wrap the raw bytes as UnparseableExtraFieldData rather than exercising our merge logic properly.

Actually, if the header ID is well-formed but simply unregistered, ExtraFieldUtils would create an UnrecognizedExtraField instance carrying that same headerId, matching our SimpleExtraField's ID and thus triggering the existing-field merge branch through legitimate parsing behavior.

Now I'll design the test case, starting with testSetExtra_mergesWithExistingField_local.

I'll create a ZipArchiveEntry, add an existing extra field with a known header id and payload, then capture its encoded local extra bytes as the baseline before constructing new well-formed extra bytes with the same header id but a different payload to test the merge behavior.

I'm calling setExtra with these new bytes and verifying the existing SimpleExtraField instance gets mutated in place with the new payload, while confirming the extra field lookup by id still returns the same object reference — this validates that the low-level construction matches the documented APPNOTE format (two-byte header id, two-byte length, then payload) described in the class Javadoc.

I also want to test the analogous merge branch for setCentralDirectoryExtra when an existing field is already present: after adding it, calling setCentralDirectoryExtra with a different payload should update that same existing field's central directory data. I'm distinguishing this from the separate existing==null branch, which is exercised differently when extraFields is null and setExtraFields creates a fresh entry rather than going through the merge loop.

For full loop branch coverage, I want a scenario combining both cases: an entry already has field 0x1111, and I call setExtra with bytes containing two fields -- one matching 0x1111 (triggers the merge/existing!=null path) and one with a new id 0x9999 (triggers addExtraField inside the loop for existing==null). This test verifies both fields end up correctly merged or added, giving two total extra fields on the entry.

I should keep the test suite thorough but avoid bloat, so I'll finalize it now. I'm also planning focused tests for equals() covering same-object, null, and other comparison branches.

I should also test isolating individual field differences while holding others equal, plus verify a full match works using the copy constructor and that null comments are treated equivalently to empty strings.

Thinking about testing name-null-vs-not-null equality, I realize the null-name trick doesn't actually work: setName(null) still falls back to the superclass's original non-null name through getName(), so equals() can never truly hit a null myName branch through any legitimate construction path. That branch looks genuinely unreachable given the class's invariants, which seems worth noting rather than assuming it's testable.

Given this, I'll skip forcing that dead branch — doing so would require invasive reflection hacks into ZipEntry's private fields — and instead focus effort on covering the other equals() comparisons: method, size, crc, compressedSize, external/internal attributes, platform, gpb, and extra fields. With limited time, I'll write a handful of representative false-case tests plus a true-case, enough to exercise each short-circuit point in the &&-chain without exhaustively covering every permutation.

I'll also cover the same-object, null, and different-class early returns, a name/comment defaulting case, a fully-equal clone-based true case, and one deeper chain check like differing size to confirm the chain proceeds past earlier conditions. Then I'll add simple getter/setter tests for versionMadeBy, versionRequired, and rawFlag.

Now I need a helper that builds little-endian encoded extra field bytes from a header ID and payload. Writing helper method...

I also need a concatenation helper for combining byte arrays. Writing concat helper...

Now I'm checking that my SimpleExtraField test class properly implements the ZipExtraField interface with matching method signatures, particularly around exception declarations -- since Java allows overriding methods to omit declared checked exceptions if they don't actually throw them, this should compile fine even without full throws clauses.

I'm trying to recall the exact interface from Apache Commons Compress: it defines getHeaderId, getLocalFileDataLength, getCentralDirectoryLength, getLocalFileDataData, getCentralDirectoryData, and two parse methods (parseFromLocalFileData and parseFromCentralDirectoryData) both throwing ZipException. This matches my assumption and aligns with how ZipArchiveEntry uses these fields.

UnparseableExtraFieldData also needs to implement the ZipExtraField interface consistently. Then for GeneralPurposeBit, I just need a default constructor, an equals method used elsewhere, and a clone method needed for the copy constructor.

For UnixStat, I'm assuming LINK_FLAG is a public static final int constant matching the standard unix symlink flag, consistent with the known commons-compress API alongside FILE_FLAG, DIR_FLAG, and PERM_MASK. I'm fairly confident this is correct. I also need to check the ArchiveEntry.SIZE_UNKNOWN constant value.

I'm referencing ArchiveEntry.SIZE_UNKNOWN (likely -1L) from the org.apache.commons.compress.archivers package, then finalizing the test code with explanatory comments for assumptions, plus a summary table. I also need to account for PowerMockRunner applying at the class level so it covers all tests including the static-mock ones, and I'm adding the necessary PowerMock imports for the runner and class preparation annotations.

For mocking ExtraFieldUtils.parse as a static method that throws a checked ZipException, PowerMockito should handle this fine since the method's throws clause already declares it, and no import is needed for ExtraFieldUtils since it's in the same package.

Then I'm writing a test that calls setExtra with bad bytes and expects a RuntimeException whose message mentions "Error parsing extra fields", and doing the same for setCentralDirectoryExtra since it wraps the exception similarly.

I also confirm that since ZipArchiveEntry(String) doesn't call parse internally, mocking the static parse method only affects the explicit call we make, so the test scope is safe.

Now I'm defining a minimal SimpleExtraField helper class implementing ZipExtraField with local and central data fields...

Finishing the parsing method, then I'll assemble the complete test file with all discussed test cases organized with comments, trimming some redundant equals tests to keep around 45 solid test methods for reasonable coverage.

For creating test entries with actual byte content, I need to write a temp file with FileOutputStream to give it nonzero size, since createTempFile alone produces empty files. I need to import FileOutputStream and declare the test method to throw Exception for IOException handling, then verify the protected no-arg constructor before writing out the final answer.

Since protected constructors are accessible within the same package regardless of subclassing, I can directly instantiate ZipArchiveEntry with its no-arg constructor and assert that the name defaults to an empty string. I'm also considering adding a test for the copy constructor that checks the general purpose bit default behavior.

Adding a second copy-constructor test confirming the clone is a distinct object but equal in value, covering both branches of that ternary. Now I'm turning to the ZipEntry-based constructor, planning tests for both the null-extra branch (calling the no-arg setExtra) and the non-null-extra branch (parsing extra fields via ExtraFieldUtils).

I also verify the deflated method carries through and that the extra field parses correctly into an UnrecognizedExtraField with the matching header id. With both branches, method assignment, and size covered, I'm ready to finalize and write out the complete test code along with a concise summary table mapping methods to branches.
